summary: Steel fire tower on Mudlick Mountain in Sam A. Baker State Park, Wayne County, MO; standing by 1935, reported 85 ft; last dated mention 1972-73; current condition not confirmed.

facts.design: Steel four-legged tower with an enclosed observing room at the top (1963 NGS description)
facts.status_note: No source read confirms the tower's condition after a 1972-73 road-work mention; present condition not confirmed
facts.agency: Missouri Conservation Commission (towersite owner per 1947-48 state manual); located in Sam A. Baker State Park

staffing.status: a towerman was on duty in January 1958 (unnamed); no later staffing record found

access.note: Inside Sam A. Baker State Park. MDC lists hiking loops that reach the natural area. No source read says the tower itself is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: MDC: the 1.5 mile Shut-Ins Trail loop and the 12 mile Mudlick Mountain hiking loop provide access to the natural area.

events.note: Already standing by July 4, 1935, when a newspaper describes it as the great steel fire tower on one of the park's highest points
1947-48 state manual lists the towersite as owned by the Missouri Conservation Commission
A towerman at Mudlick discovered a fire (reported January 1958); no name given
Fire burned eight acres of a Wayne County farm and took two hours to bring under control; reported January 10, 1958 (fire date not given)
National Geodetic Survey station description: about 100 ft tall, four-legged steel structure
FY1972-73 state report: road reshaped at the tower; last dated mention found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 85 ft (two state annual reports; a 1938 newspaper item describes an 85-foot vantage point in the tower), 80 ft (a July 1935 article) and about 100 ft (1963 survey). We used 85 ft, the figure both state reports give. The sources do not explain the gap.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives a build year; the July 1935 article is the earliest mention. A search snippet from AllTrails says the CCC built the tower in 1936, but the page returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited and the 1936 date conflicts with the 1935 article. Missouri Life and The Prospect pages (both HTTP 403) reportedly say the tower is still used to spot smoke; not verified, not cited. Record access was 'unknown'; set to public for the park, climbing not confirmed. Staffing as_of 1958 is the last staffing mention found. Fact-check 2026-10-09: facts.status changed from 'standing' to 'unknown', because no source read confirms the tower's present condition.
